real_chain: Unbound source FileSystemCAS object is exported as an import archive.
Two concurrent tenant-scoped FileSystemCAS receiver calls enter actual import_subgraph and reservation/publication code for the same artifact.
The first actual artifact lease covers the pending ownership transaction and pauses before default manifest publication; the contender attempts the same lease and is blocked.
After release, the winner publishes the manifest/owner receipt; the other import is refused as a foreign exact view.
Fresh winner and loser FileSystemCAS instances reread bytes/manifests and verify winner-only ownership and loser refusal.
adversarial_controls: Removal control routes the competing worker to a different lock stripe; the preserved runtime markers do not hide the race and the test fails at the publication-entered assertion.
Fresh losing tenant cannot claim ownership, has no exact view, and raises ArtifactOwnershipError on read.
Winner's payload bytes and source manifest are checked after a fresh receiver open; source remains unbound.

The positive module suite retains existing malformed-input, staged-import, selected-view, foreign-owner, and integrity controls; the 57-case result is module-wide and not a count attributable solely to the new test.

limitations: The contenders share one in-process CAS coordinator and temporary local filesystem; this does not establish cross-process or production-deployment serialization.
The adversarial control routes around the selected artifact stripe in the test; it does not remove or patch the production lease implementation.
No external transfer permission, legal right, issuer authority, production currentness, T2 protected-positive fact, or production custody claim is created.
The test does not prove internal critical-section overlap under every scheduler; it directly observes one contender attempt while the winner holds the actual stripe.
